The core innovation lies in combining zero-shot phrase grounding with fine-tuned pose estimation to enable robust player tracking in tennis doubles. The system uses GroundingDINO for initial detection, followed by YOLO-Pose for keypoint localization. This dual-stage pipeline ensures accurate player identification even under varying lighting or occlusion. The annotation schema defines four categories—player info, positional info, frame info, and rally info—which collectively provide rich semantic context. These primitives map into GSE’s state-transition models via player tracking and shot classification. GSI leverages this structured data for Bayesian inference on game states. The failure mode arises when visual cues are insufficient, particularly for P3/P4 players due to camera angle or motion blur. Transferability to football is limited due to differing tactical structures and fewer standardized annotations.
